scenario.fault_family: BGP config error (wrong remote-as on a neighbor)
scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Since a config push this morning, the BGP session between
spine_router_0_1 and leaf_router_0_1 will not come up: it cycles
without ever reaching Established, and the leaf's log shows its OPEN
being rejected by the spine with an AS error. Every other session in
the fabric is Established, all interfaces are UP, and users report at
most a brief blip -- pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) and pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) still
reach each other. Find the fault.

injection.action: misconfigure the remote-as of the leaf_router_0_1 neighbor

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: spine_router_0_1 BGP neighbor remote-as
Mechanism: spine_router_0_1 (AS 65101) peers with leaf_router_0_1 at
  172.16.0.11, whose real AS is 65201. The neighbor statement was
  changed to `remote-as 65999`, so when the leaf's OPEN arrives
  announcing AS 65201, spine_router_0_1 rejects it with an OPEN error
  (Bad Peer AS) notification and the session can never establish --
  it cycles between Idle/Active/OpenSent. The CLOS fabric is
  redundant: leaf_router_0_1 still peers with spine_router_0_0, so
  both host prefixes stay reachable and the impact is loss of the
  second spine path for leaf_router_0_1, not an outage.
Localization: spine_router_0_1 (the misconfigured side; leaf_router_0_1's
  own config is unchanged and correct)
Root cause: neighbor 172.16.0.11 configured with remote-as 65999
  instead of 65201 on spine_router_0_1
Fix: set the neighbor's remote-as back to 65201 on spine_router_0_1
  (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
Correct the remote-as on spine_router_0_1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router bgp 65101"
 -c "neighbor 172.16.0.11 remote-as 65201"`
Note: the injection changed only the running config; the intended
config is still intact in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so `service frr restart`
on spine_router_0_1 is an equally correct fix.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a wrong remote-AS value in spine_router_0_1's BGP configuration for its neighbor
toward leaf_router_0_1. The physical link between these two devices uses the /31 pair
172.16.0.10 (spine eth2) / 172.16.0.11 (leaf eth1), and both ends have IP connectivity.
leaf_router_0_1 correctly lists neighbor 172.16.0.10 remote-as 65101 (which matches
spine_router_0_1's true AS number). However, spine_router_0_1 was configured — presumably
altered during this morning's config push — with neighbor 172.16.0.11 remote-as 65999
instead of the correct 65201.

The mechanism is standard BGP OPEN validation: when leaf_router_0_1 opens a TCP session
to port 179 and sends its OPEN message declaring AS 65201, spine_router_0_1 compares that
value against its configured remote-as 65999, finds a mismatch, and immediately sends a
BGP NOTIFICATION with error code 2 (OPEN Message Error), sub-code 2 (Bad Peer AS). This
is confirmed directly by the vtysh output: "Notification sent (OPEN Message Error/Bad Peer AS)"
with 6 sent NOTIFICATIONs and 0 received, exactly matching the symptom that "the leaf's log
shows its OPEN being rejected by the spine with an AS error." The session then falls back to
Idle and retries every 120 seconds, producing the cycling behaviour observed.

All other sessions in the fabric are Established because their remote-as values were not
touched by the push (spine_router_0_1↔super_spine and spine_router_0_1↔leaf_router_0_0
are both up with correct AS numbers).

Root cause: the config push this morning set neighbor 172.16.0.11 remote-as 65999 on
spine_router_0_1 instead of the correct remote-as 65201.

Corrective fix: on spine_router_0_1, replace the erroneous statement —
  no neighbor 172.16.0.11 remote-as 65999
  neighbor 172.16.0.11 remote-as 65201
The session will reach Established on the next connect cycle without any restart.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names spine_router_0_1 as the misconfigured device (wrong neighbor remote-as) and describes fixes to apply there.

per_axis.rationale: Explicitly identifies the BGP neighbor remote-as mismatch on spine_router_0_1 (configured 65999 instead of the correct 65201).

per_axis.axis: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: only the spine_router_0_1 <-> leaf_router_0_1 session is affected while links are UP and all other sessions are Established
per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly states the local link is up, only the spine<->leaf session cycles due to the bad remote-as, and all other BGP sessions are Established, matching the required symptom distinction.

per_axis.axis: bonus-cites-mismatch-values: cites the configured remote-as 65999 vs leaf_router_0_1's actual AS 65201
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly notes spine_router_0_1 is configured with remote-as 65999 while leaf_router_0_1 announces AS 65201, identifying the mismatch.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-leaf: notes leaf_router_0_1's own configuration is correct/unchanged, so the misconfiguration is on the spine side
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states leaf_router_0_1's config is correct/unchanged (shows correct neighbor remote-as) and attributes the misconfiguration to spine_router_0_1's incorrect remote-as setting.
Proposes removing the wrong neighbor remote-as and configuring neighbor 172.16.0.11 remote-as 65201 on spine_router_0_1, which matches the expected fix.
